stories.new_fact: Microsoft says BNY and Microsoft completed an agentic negotiation of a U.S. Treasury trade.

stories.previous_coverage: Differs from Nov. 18’s regulator-risk segment and uses lane 6 markets/trading support rather than lane 8 resilience.

stories.new_fact: Microsoft made Microsoft-Decision 1.1 generally available, added multimodal support, and positions it for routing, classification, prioritization, verification, and workflow control.
stories.new_takeaway: General availability is a reason for a bounded, labeled-work-item comparison, not proof that a low-cost model is suitable for consequential bank decisions.
stories.why_now: The enterprise availability and capability update were announced November 17.
stories.previous_coverage: Different from Nov. 18 GPT-6.2 coverage: this is a task-specific decision-model access change rather than a new general frontier-model comparison.
stories.uncertainty: Microsoft provides no independent or task-level error, escalation, correction-cost, or quality comparison in the announcement.
stories.watch: Independent benchmarks, documented task errors, latency/cost evidence, and implementation outcomes.
stories.frontier_bar: New capability with enterprise general availability; access shift.

editorial_review.notes: Five fresh developments dated November 17–18. No substantive carryovers. Home lending is MBS disclosure operations, banking AI is lane-six markets support with company/vendor evidence, and frontier AI is an enterprise decision-model availability change. Markets and weather are routine. The script is 1,713 spoken words with 27.7% COHOST contribution; all turns are under 100 words and thirteen COHOST questions receive useful answers.
